candidates.title: Draft booking and provider updates

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a draft customer or provider update from an operator-supplied booking status and flag missing or failed updates.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How can n8n help automate booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates, and customer alerts?

ease.reason: A student can test status-to-message drafts with fictional bookings, but no supplied reference supports live bookings or notifications.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small on-demand service operators might pay for fewer missed updates; the post establishes no buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can map fictional statuses to draft notices; event handling, payment accuracy and external APIs remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed draft loop can apply fixed status rules, but a person must verify payment facts and approve every message; execution is unsupported.

evidence.reason: The retained post span requests booking confirmations, provider assignment notices, payment updates, customer alerts and failure handling, but gives no frequency or corroboration.

experimentPlan.output: Draft one booking or provider status message and flag missing status fields.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator enters a fictional booking row for a draft run.
steps: Read the supplied status fields.
Match the status to a proposed message template.
Flag missing or contradictory fields.
Draft a notice without sending it.
Show the draft and flags to an operator.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed fictional row, verify that the selected template matches its status and that missing fields produce a visible flag.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies and verifies all fields, checks payment state, and approves any message; no live API or customer data is used.
unverified: Live booking and payment integrations are unsupported.
Status rules, message templates and event triggers are design assumptions.
Duplicate prevention and retry behavior are untested.

candidates.reason: Concrete discussion chore assessed as a narrow proposed experiment; provisional scores remain below the threshold of 6.
